podcast.title: Ian Watkins Murdered in Prison (2025) – Stabbed by Fellow Inmates
podcast.body: Ian Watkins, former frontman of Lostprophets who had been convicted of child sexual abuse, was stabbed to death by other inmates in a British prison in 2025. "Stabbed to death by other inmates in a British prison."

podcast.title: Band Members' Reaction
podcast.body: The other five members of Lostprophets were entirely innocent and unaware of Ian Watkins's heinous activities. They were absolutely horrified and devastated by the news, unable to comprehend that the person with whom they had toured extensively was involved in such sick and twisted crimes. "They were absolutely horrified and devastated with this news and knowledge."

podcast.title: Band's Success and Rise to Fame
podcast.body: Lostprophets, a Welsh band that emerged in the late 1990s, achieved international success with their second album, "Start Something," released in 2004. They subsequently released more albums, embarked on numerous tours, including the Warped Tour, and received several awards. "They were banned that came out of whales in the late 90s and broke through internationally with their second album, something called Start Something in 2004."

podcast.title: Guilty Plea and Conviction
podcast.body: Ian Watkins initially denied all charges. However, by the time his trial began on November 26, 2013, he pleaded guilty to the sexual offenses, though he maintained a not-guilty plea to the count of rape. He was identified by officials as the "most dangerous sex offender they had ever seen," describing him as a "committed, organized, pedophile." "He initially denied all charges, but by the time things went to trial in November 26, 2013, he pleaded guilty to the sexual offenses, but not guilty to the count of rape."

podcast.title: Ian Watkins's Arrest and Charges
podcast.body: The band's career abruptly ended on December 19, 2012, when singer Ian Watkins was arrested. He was charged with 13 sexual offenses against children, including the attempted rape of a one-year-old. Additionally, Watkins faced charges for distributing images of these offenses and for "extreme animal pornography involving a child." "This one singer Ian Watkins was arrested and charged with 13 sexual offenses against children. That included the attempted rape of a one-year-old."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sentence and Accomplices
podcast.body: Ian Watkins was sentenced to 29 years in jail, facing an additional six years of supervised release if he survives his prison term. He had two female accomplices in his crimes, one of whom was the mother of one of the child victims; their identities were protected to safeguard the children involved, and they were sentenced to 14 and 17 years in prison, respectively. A third woman, Watkins's ex-girlfriend, went to trial but was cleared of all charges in January 2015. "Watkins was sentenced to 29 years in jail. If he makes it out, he faces another six years of supervised release."
